description: A Metal renderer for Minecraft Java on Apple Silicon: HDR terrain lighting, shadows, volumetrics, water reflections and TAA at native Retina resolution

mods.name: Tilelight
mods.description: A Metal renderer for Minecraft on Apple Silicon.

releases.notes:
Tilelight now draws and lights terrain on Metal in the Nether and the End, and vanilla's lighting effects work on Metal-lit terrain. Experimental: expect rough edges.

![Nether: vanilla terrain vs Tilelight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maarao/tilelight/main/docs/dims-nether-tilelight.png)

## What's new
- **Nether and End on Metal.** Terrain is lit in HDR from vanilla's per-dimension lighting, so it stays faithful to each dimension's palette but gains contrast. A hue-preserving tonemap keeps lava orange.
- **Lava glow in the Nether.** Lava, glowstone and fire glow softly into the dark air.
- **Vanilla's lighting effects now apply to Metal-lit terrain:** Brightness slider, night vision (and conduit power), Darkness, boss-fog darkening, torch flicker and lightning flashes. With no effect active, the Overworld looks exactly as in 0.1.0.
- Fixes: the shadow map and anti-aliasing history now reset when you change world or dimension.

Cost on a base M5 MacBook Pro (3456×2168): about 0.25–0.4 ms per frame over vanilla terrain in the Nether and End, which still run at ~245 and ~273 fps. Details and measurements: [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/maarao/tilelight/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Requirements
- An Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later). Tilelight stays off on other machines.
- Minecraft Java 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5+, Fabric API
- **Graphics API set to Vulkan** in video settings. Tilelight stays off on OpenGL.

## Install
Put `tilelight-0.2.0.jar` in `mods/`, replacing any older Tilelight jar. You can add `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` to the JVM arguments to silence Java's native-access warning. Settings are in `config/tilelight.json`; see the [README](https://github.com/maarao/tilelight#use).

## Known limitations
- Doesn't work alongside Sodium, Iris or other mods that replace terrain rendering.
- Sun shadows, sun shafts and water reflections of the sun are Overworld-only.

mods.name: Tilelight
mods.description: A Metal renderer for Minecraft on Apple Silicon.

releases.notes:
First public build. Experimental: expect rough edges.

![Sunset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maarao/tilelight/main/docs/look2-sunset.png)

Tilelight moves parts of each Minecraft frame onto Metal: opaque terrain lit in HDR, sun shadows, volumetric haze and sun shafts, screen-space water reflections, bloom, and TAA plus MetalFX upscaling. On a base M5 MacBook Pro at 3456×2168, render distance 16, it runs at ~125 fps with everything on (vanilla: ~158 fps).

## Requirements
- An Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or later). Tilelight stays off on other machines.
- Minecraft Java 26.3, Fabric Loader 0.19.5+, Fabric API
- **Graphics API set to Vulkan** in video settings. Tilelight stays off on OpenGL.

## Install
Put `tilelight-0.1.0.jar` in `mods/`. You can add `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` to the JVM arguments to silence Java's native-access warning.

Settings are in `config/tilelight.json`. See the [README](https://github.com/maarao/tilelight#use).

## Known limitations
- Doesn't work alongside Sodium, Iris or other mods that replace terrain rendering.
- Metal terrain and lighting are Overworld-only. The Nether and the End stay vanilla.
